clusters.label: DDR_ECC
clusters.representative_signature: DDR_ECC | DDR: ECC uncorrectable error ; FW: Memtest mismatch ; DDR: DDR PHY register snapshot ; SYSTEM: DDR subsystem failure ; DDR: ECC corrected errors rising ; DDR: CDC synchronizer glitch ; DDR: Read retry invoked

hypotheses.root_cause: A clock-domain-crossing synchronizer glitch in the DDR controller's read FIFO (rd_fifo, PHY->ctrl crossing) on ch=1 at 2400 MHz corrupted read data. The errors grew from correctable ECC errors to a read retry, then a multi-bit uncorrectable error on bank 6, and finally a FW memtest mismatch.
hypotheses.rationale:
Causal chain: ECC correctable errors rising on ch1 bank6 (8503 ms) -> CDC synchronizer glitch rd_fifo phy->ctrl (8526 ms) -> read retry ch1 (8621 ms) -> ECC UE ch1 bank6 syndrome 0xF709 (8855 ms) -> FW memtest mismatch with 17/32 bits wrong across all byte lanes (8910 ms) -> SYSTEM FATAL DDR subsystem failure (8992 ms). The only cause marker anywhere in the logs is the DDR CDC synchronizer glitch line. It is on the read path and comes about 330 ms before the uncorrectable error, followed by a read retry on the same channel. The corrupted word has 17 bits flipped in both directions across all 4 byte lanes. That looks like wrong or garbled data captured at a crossing, not a cell fault or a stuck lane. The ecc_ue counter staying at 0 after a logged UE also suggests the PHY->ctrl handoff was corrupted.

FW's RC_DDR_TIMING_VIOLATION call comes from the historian's match to run 000016, and FW cannot see DDR logs. The DDR specialist points out that 000016 had an explicit "Timing parameter violation" line, which is missing here. The 0.98 similarity comes from the shared generic lines (ECC, memtest, snapshot, fatal), not from the line that identifies the cause.

PMU shows VCORE steady with droop_cnt=0 and no events. Thermal is flat at 53–57 °C.

Confidence is held to moderate for three reasons:
- Corrected ECC errors were already rising before the glitch (136 at 8116 ms; the delta=107 WARN at 8503 ms), so a slowly worsening problem may have come first.
- The DDR rails (VDDQ/VDD2/PHY) are not monitored, so droop on those rails can't be ruled out.
- The PHY snapshot is not decoded. (1 of 4 specialists pointed at this cause.)
recommended_actions: Decode the ch=1 PHY register snapshot (0x50000FDF-0x5000105B): look for CDC/FIFO status, sticky error bits, and DQS/DQ delay values that would separate a CDC glitch from a timing or training problem.

Re-run at 2400 MHz with CDC/rd_fifo error counters and a logic-analyzer trigger on the PHY->ctrl synchronizer. Repeat at a lower DRAM frequency or with a deeper synchronizer or FIFO setting and check whether the failure goes away.
Add VDDQ/VDD2/PHY rail telemetry to rule out DDR-rail droop around 8100-8900 ms.
Find out why ecc_ue stays at 0 after the logged UE (a counter-path CDC issue or a readout bug).
Check whether the CDC glitch line also appeared in run 000016, to judge whether that incident's label is reliable.

trace.output: DDR: Look at the ch=1 PHY register snapshot and DDR logs from 8855-8992 ms. Is there a timing violation, such as training/eye margin drift, tRCD/tRP/tWR violations, or DQS/DQ delay changes, at 2400 MHz on ch=1? Is the ECC error correctable or uncorrectable, and does it stay on one rank/bank/address or is it spread out (single-bit vs multi-bit)? Compare with run 000016 (RC_DDR_TIMING_VIOLATION).; FW: For the memtest mismatch at addr=0x957A5CF9 (expected 0xDEADBEEF, got 0xF4752381), which bits flipped, how many, and what pattern do they show? Which memtest pattern or phase was running, and did firmware change the DDR frequency, timing parameters, or refresh settings shortly before 8910 ms?; PMU: Between 8800 and 8992 ms, were there any voltage droops, DVFS transitions, or regulator faults on the DDR VDDQ/VDD2 or PHY supply rails, or rail changes tied to the 2400 MHz operating point, that could reduce DDR timing margin on ch=1?; THERMAL: What were the DRAM and SoC temperatures near the DDR PHY in the 8800-8992 ms window? Did temperature rise quickly or cross a threshold that should have triggered a refresh-rate derate or DDR throttling that didn't happen?
trace.note: This is a critical DDR_ECC failure on ch=1 at 2400 MHz, with the firmware memtest mismatch showing up first. The closest past incident (run 000016, sim 0.98) traced to RC_DDR_TIMING_VIOLATION, so DDR is the main target. FW can tell us the bit-flip pattern and any timing or frequency changes it made. PMU covers supply droop and THERMAL covers temperature drift, the two most likely upstream causes of lost timing margin. NOC, PCIE and BOOT look less related given the other similar incidents, so they're left out.

Root causes the DDR specialist can recognise:
- RC_DDR_TIMING_VIOLATION: A DRAM timing parameter is violated at the configured frequency  (tell-tales: timing parameter violation, trfc, trcd)
- RC_DDR_TRAINING_EDGE: Read/write training converged on a marginal edge  (tell-tales: read training margin low, margin_ps)
- RC_PMU_DROOP_UNDER_LOAD: VDDQ droop under load corrupts DRAM accesses  (tell-tales: fast droop event, rail=vddq)
- RC_DDR_CDC_GLITCH: Clock-domain-crossing synchroniser glitch in the controller  (tell-tales: cdc synchronizer glitch, cdc)

RC_DDR_TIMING_VIOLATION (0.55): Bit analysis: 0xDEADBEEF XOR 0xF4752381 = 0x2AD89D6E, so 17 of 32 bits flipped. Per byte: [31:24] 0x2A (3 bits), [23:16] 0xD8 (4), [15:8] 0x9D (5), [7:0] 0x6E (5). Bits flipped in both directions (1→0 and 0→1) in every byte lane. That is not one stuck bit, one stuck lane or a single-bit upset. The returned word looks like random or wrong-data corruption, which fits data captured at the wrong sampling point or read from the wrong beat/burst, not a cell retention fault. Also, the address 0x957A5CF9 is not word-aligned (it ends in 0x9). FW logged only one error in 0–9000 ms: the memtest mismatch
trace.note: From the FW side I see no firmware fault: no FW error before the mismatch, FW kept running normally afterwards, and FW logged no change to DDR frequency, timing or refresh before 8910 ms.
